rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa says the Companions hastened to obey the Prophet, competed for his ablution water, lowered their voices, and revered him more than companions of any king he had visited; he urges acceptance of the Prophet’s sound proposal.
rows.anchor: قال فرجع عروة إلى أصحابه وقال أي قوم والله لقد وفدت على الملوك ووفدت على قيصر وكسرى والنجاشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man from Banu Kinana approaches after the Prophet identifies his people as honoring sacrificial camels; seeing the animals sent out and hearing the pilgrims’ talbiya, he says they should not be barred from the House.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هذا فلان وهو من قوم يعظمون البدن فابعثوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makraz b. Hafs argues with the Prophet, then Suhayl b. Amr arrives to propose a written settlement; the Prophet remarks that their affair has become easier.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قد سهل عليكم أمركم فقال اكتب بيننا وبينك كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhayl rejects the phrases “the Merciful” and “Muhammad, Messenger of God”; Muhammad insists on his messengership but accepts “in Your name, O God” and “Muhammad b. Abd Allah,” erasing the title himself when Ali refuses.
rows.anchor: فقال سهيل لو كنا نعلم أنك رسول الله ما صددناك عن البيت ولا قاتلناك ولكن اكتب محمد بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treaty suspends war for ten years, guarantees safe passage and security, bars theft and treachery, and lets tribes enter either Muhammad’s or Quraysh’s pact.
rows.anchor: واصطلحا على وضع الحرب عن الناس عشر سنين يأمن فيهن الناس ويكف بعضهم عن بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuzāʿa joins Muhammad’s pact and Banu Bakr joins Quraysh’s; Quraysh postpone the Muslims’ pilgrimage to the following year, when they may stay three days with only sheathed swords and travelers’ arms.
rows.anchor: تواثبت خزاعة فقالوا نحن في عقد محمد وعهده، وتواثبت بنو بكر فقالوا نحن في عقد قريش وعهدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treaty requires returning Quraysh men who come to Muhammad even if Muslim, while not returning Muhammad’s men who go to Quraysh; the Prophet says God will provide an outlet for anyone sincere in Islam.
rows.anchor: فقال سهيل على أنه لا يأتيك منا رجل وإن كان على دينك إلا رددته إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhayl demands that his shackled son Abu Jandal be returned; the Prophet says the treaty is not yet concluded and asks for an exception, but Abu Jandal is left pleading with Muslims despite severe torture.
rows.anchor: فبينا هم كذلك إذ جاء أبو جندل بن سهيل بن عمرو يرسف في قيوده وقد خرج من أسفل مكة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar questions why Muslims accept a humiliating settlement and whether the promised pilgrimage was delayed; the Prophet answers that he never promised it would happen that year and that they will visit next year.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب والله ما شككت مذ أسلمت إلا يومئذ فأتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet sacrifices and shaves, the Companions follow; when believing women arrive as emigrants, the verse on testing and not returning them is revealed.
rows.anchor: فنحر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بدنة فدعا بحالقه فحلق شعره ثم جاءه نسوة مؤمنات

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits through Burayda b. Sufyan from Muhammad b. Kaʿb that Ali wrote the treaty; he hesitated to replace “Messenger of God,” and the Prophet promised him an equivalent trial before accepting the agreed wording.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب أن كاتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في هذا الصلح كان علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ibn Ishaq’s account, Quraysh’s envoys take Abu Basir back under the treaty; he kills one, escapes the other, and the Prophet calls him a war-stirrer before Abu Basir flees to the coast.
rows.anchor: فضربه به حتى برد وفر الآخر حتى بلغ المدينة فدخل المسجد يعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jandal and other Muslim escapees gather with Abu Basir and attack Quraysh’s Syria caravans; Quraysh then ask the Prophet to receive the defectors safely, and he sends for them.
rows.anchor: وانفلت منهم أبو جندل بن سهيل فلحق بأبي بصير فلا يخرج من قريش رجل قد أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long report in Tafsir al-Qummi says the Companions refused to sacrifice and shave before pilgrimage rites; Umm Salama advised the Prophet to do so himself, and they followed after he did.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في حديث طويل أوردنا صدره في أول البحث قال وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the Umm Salama episode occurs in other Shiʿi and Sunni reports and that al-Tabrisi’s abridged version draws on al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasaʾi through Marwan and al-Miswar.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو مروي في روايات أخر من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa reports that a Companion called Hudaybiyya no victory because Muslims were barred from the House and two Muslims returned; the Prophet calls it the greatest victory because Quraysh conceded, sought settlement, and God returned Muslims safely and rewarded.
rows.anchor: أخرج البيهقي عن عروة قال أقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الحديبية راجعا فقال رجل من أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: The Prophet recalls the peril of Uhud and the Confederates to show how much safer the Hudaybiyya return was; the Muslims accept his judgment and say he knows God and events better.
rows.anchor: أنسيتم يوم أحد إذ تصعدون ولا تلوون على أحد وأنا أدعوكم في أخراكم؟ أنسيتم يوم الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that many reports recount Hudaybiyya and that the accounts given here are only selections.
rows.anchor: أقول والأحاديث في قصة الحديبية كثيرة وما أوردناه طرف منها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in Tafsir al-Qummi says the Prophet had neither a sin nor an intention to sin; God bore the sins of his Shiʿa and forgave them through him.
rows.anchor: قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام قول الله في كتابه { ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر } قال ما كان له ذنب

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida explains that Meccan polytheists treated the Prophet’s call to exclusive worship as his “sin”; after the conquest some converted, others left, and the rest could no longer oppose tawhid, so their grievance was overcome.
rows.anchor: قال الرضا عليه السلام لم يكن أحد عند مشركي مكة أعظم ذنبا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from Mansur b. Hazim that the Prophet continued saying he feared punishment if he disobeyed God until Surat al-Fath was revealed, after which he stopped.
rows.anchor: عن منصور بن حازم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ما ترك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم { إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Sunni routes also transmit that report but criticizes it because it assumes the verse’s “sin” means disobedience, which conflicts with prophetic infallibility.
rows.anchor: والحديث لا يخلو من شيء لأنه مبني على كون المراد بالذنب في الآية هو المعصية المنافية للعصمة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jamil reports that Abu Abdallah glosses the tranquility placed in believers’ hearts as faith; the author reads this as interpreting the following increase of faith as the meaning of tranquility and notes parallel reports.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده إلى جميل قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين } قال الإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Amr al-Zubayri’s report says faith comprises action, while speech is one part of it; God assigns distinct faith duties to each limb, and fulfilling them completely yields complete faith and Paradise, while betrayal leaves faith deficient.
rows.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن أبي عمرو الزبيري عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له أيها العالم أخبرني أي الأعمال أفضل عند الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Faith has complete, deficient, and increasing degrees; the Imam cites 9:124 and 18:13, arguing that variation makes believers differ in rank, while completeness leads to Paradise and deficiency to Hell.
rows.anchor: فقال قول الله عز وجل { وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four opening oaths exemplify world governance through causes on land, sea, and in the sky, completed by angels as intermediaries; together they swear by the general means through which cosmic affairs are administered.
rows.anchor: فالآيات في معنى أن يقال أقسم بعامة الأسباب التي يتمم بها أمر التدبير في العالم

rows.speaker: علي عليه أفضل السلام
rows.claim: Traditions from both Shiʿi and Sunni routes attribute the preceding interpretation of the four oaths to Ali.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد من طرق الخاصة والعامة عن علي عليه أفضل السلام تفسير الآيات الأربع بما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Razi says all four oaths most likely refer to winds; the author rejects this as remote and prefers the broader account of varied causes as more eloquent.
rows.anchor: وعن الفخر الرازي في التفسير الكبير أن الأقرب حمل الآيات الأربع جميعا على الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer is that what the Qurʾan or Prophet promises about resurrection and recompense is true, and that judgment will certainly occur, rewarding good and evil deeds accordingly.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أقسم بكذا وكذا أن الذي توعدونه - وهو الذي يعدهم القرآن أو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بما أنزل إليه - من يوم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “what you are promised,” the particle “ma” may be a relative pronoun with an omitted antecedent pronoun, or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: { ما } موصولة، والضمير العائد إليها محذوف أي الذين توعدونه، أو مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may derive from promise, supported by the following reference to recompense, or from threat, supported by the cited poetic line about warning those who fear the threat.
rows.anchor: وقيل من الايعاد كما يؤيده قوله فذكر بالقرآن من يخاف وعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the promised matter truthful is a figurative attribution, as in “a pleasing life,” or “truthful” can mean possessing truth; the next clause explains the first, and “din” means recompense.
rows.anchor: وعد الوعد صادقا من المجاز في النسبة كما في قوله في عيشة راضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hubuk can mean beauty and adornment, well-formedness, or paths and wave-like patterns on water made by the wind; on the first meanings the oath is by the beautiful, adorned sky.
rows.anchor: الحبك بمعنى الحسن والزينة، وبمعنى الخلق المستوي، ويأتي جمعا لحبيكة أو حباك بمعنى الطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage’s second section rebuts idol worship and its claim of intercession; it follows proof of revelation and prophethood grounded in monotheism, and points toward resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: بيان شطر من آيات الفصل الثاني من الفصول الثلاثة في السورة تتعرض لأمر الأوثان وعبادتها بدعوى أنها ستشفع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three named idols were worshipped by pre-Islamic Arabs, who regarded them as images of female angels or divided them between angels and humans; the passage denies the idols’ and angels’ independent divinity or intercession and denies the angels’ femininity.
rows.anchor: وهي عند المشركين تماثيل للملائكة بدعوى أنهم إناث أو بعضها للملائكة وبعضها للإنسان كما قاله بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports disagree about the idols’ appearance, locations, worshippers, and why Arabs worshipped them; these accounts conflict and cannot be relied upon, so only the basic identification is certain.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلفوا في وصف صورها، وفي موضعها الذي كانت منصوبة عليه، وفي من يعبدها من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the truth of revelation and the Prophet’s mission, the rhetorical question asks what these idols are, since the audience claims they represent angels who are God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: فأخبروني عن اللات والعزى ومناة التي هي ثالثة الصنمين وغيرهما - وهي التي تدعون أنها أصنام الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is mocking and repudiating: if the idols’ angelic lords are God’s daughters while people prefer sons, do humans get sons and God daughters? Such an allocation is unjust.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكاري مشوب بالاستهزاء، وقسمة ضيزى أي جائرة غير عادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They” refers to al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat as idols; the names are assigned by people and their parents, with no revealed proof of divinity, so the verse refutes their gods for lack of evidence.
rows.anchor: ضمير { هي } للات والعزى ومناة أولها بما هي أصنام، وضمير { سميتموها } للأسماء وتسمية الأسماء جعلها أسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ma” may be relative or a verbal noun, and desire means the soul’s sensual inclination; the clause condemns following falsehood and reinforces the absence of proof, while the guidance clause is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: { ما } موصولة والضمير العائد إليها محذوف أي الذي تهواه النفس، وقيل مصدرية والتقدير هوى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding terms are glossed variously: rafraf may be cushions; khudr is the plural of green describing rafraf; abqari has been read as rugs, carpets, embroidered cloth, or brocade.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي الوسائد، وقيل غير ذلك، والخضر جمع أخضر صفة لرفرف، والعبقري قيل الزرابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing praise celebrates God because both worlds overflow with blessings from His vast mercy; the blessed name is al-Rahman, the sura’s opening name, and baraka is abundant good issuing from Him.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يظهر أن المراد باسمه المتبارك هو الرحمن المفتتحة به السورة، والتبارك كثرة الخيرات والبركات الصادرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Possessor of majesty and honor” points to God’s beautiful names and attributes; these qualities shape His acts, from creation and wise ordering to rewarding obedience and punishing wrongdoing, so His blessings bear their imprint.
rows.anchor: ولصفات الفاعل ظهور في أفعاله وأثر فيها يرتبط به الفعل بفاعله فهو تعالى خلق الخلق ونظم النظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says angels encircle all creatures with fire and call to jinn and humans that a flame will be sent against them; the author says the same meaning is transmitted from Abu Abdallah through Musʿada b. Sadaqa and Kulayb.
rows.anchor: في المجمع وقد جاء في الخبر يحاط على الخلق بالملائكة وبلسان من نار ثم ينادون

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Dawud al-Raqqi reports Abu Abdallah’s explanation that whoever knows God sees, hears, and knows his deeds is restrained from evil; that is one who fears his Lord’s station and restrains the self from desire.
rows.anchor: عن داود الرقي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله الله عز وجل { ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان } قال من علم أن الله يراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report attributed to Abu Darda has the Prophet affirm that one fearing God’s station may still commit adultery or theft; the author doubts it because such fear cannot accompany grave sins, preferring Abu Darda’s own version that the fearful person does neither.
rows.anchor: أقول الرواية لا تخلو من شيء فإن الخوف من مقامه تعالى لا يجامع هذه الكبائر الموبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses “restraining the gaze” as houris whose radiance itself lowers the gaze.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { قاصرات الطرف } قال الحور العين يقصر الطرف عنها من ضوء نورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report through Jaʿfar b. Muhammad from his fathers to the Prophet says the houris look only at their husbands.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { قاصرات الطرف } قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ transmits that a woman in Paradise’s marrow can be seen through seventy silk garments; the author says several reports convey this meaning.
rows.anchor: أن المرأة من أهل الجنة يرى مخ ساقها من وراء سبعين حلة من حرير

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abdallah says the principle that good is repaid with good applies to disbelievers and believers, the righteous and the wicked; one receiving kindness must repay it, and should exceed the original kindness because merely matching it leaves the initiator with the merit of beginning.
rows.anchor: علي بن سالم قال سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول آية في كتاب الله مسجلة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Anas says the Prophet explained the verse as God’s promise that the reward for blessing someone with monotheism is Paradise.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites parallel wordings from the Prophet and the Imams, including that the reward for saying there is no god but God is Paradise; “I blessed him” indicates that the servant’s good is itself God’s favor to him.
rows.anchor: وقوله أنعمت عليه، إشارة إلى أن إحسان العبد بالحقيقة إحسان من الله إليه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ala b. Sayaba reports that Abu Abdallah answers people asking whether those who leave Hell will join God’s friends in Paradise: they will not, as indicated by the two gardens beneath the first pair.
rows.anchor: عن العلاء بن سيابة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قلت له إن الناس يتعجبون منا إذا قلنا يخرج قوم من النار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report through Abu Musa assigns two gardens of gold to those brought near and two gardens of silver to the companions of the right.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان } وقوله { ومن دونهما جنتان } قال جنتان من ذهب
